meta.title: Payment Timeout Recovery & Idempotency Demo | DI
meta.description: Provider-neutral payment timeout recovery demo: verify payment idempotency, prevent duplicate payments, and make AI agent payment retries evidence-bound.
meta.og_description: Did the payment fail—or did only the response fail? Compare authoritative recovery with blind-retry duplicate-effect risk.

ui.hero_title_2: or did only the response fail?
ui.hero_lead: A financial mutation can commit even when its acknowledgement disappears. A blind retry can turn uncertainty into a second effect. DI keeps the original operation identity, recovers authoritative state, and blocks an unsupported mutation.
ui.microcopy: No live provider. No real funds. Every measured result comes from the committed provider-neutral evidence pack.
ui.demo_title: One unknown state. Two very different decisions.
ui.risk_disclaimer: The blind-retry branch is an illustrative failure path. It is not a claim that any named provider or client behaves this way.
principles: One intended action retains one logical identity across timeout, retry, and worker change.
A transport timeout remains UNKNOWN until a supported source establishes committed, not committed, or still unknown.
A confirmed effect permits acceptance or stop — not a fresh mutation disguised as recovery.
ui.search_title: Common search language, one underlying failure surface.
ui.stack_title: Four projects keep different boundaries clear.
ui.stack_intro: The payment example is one external validation case. The projects remain independent and do not execute the payment.
stack: Clarify the human's actual intent before planning.
Map capability, permission, limits, risk, and unknowns before commitment.
Preserve what was decided, why, and what it depended on.
Reason about the justified transition and review the observed result.
Turn evidence into an explicit next state without inventing causality.
ui.evidence_title: Every headline number has a trail.
ui.evidence_body: The demo is a presentation layer. The source of truth remains the open repository, deterministic sandbox, machine-readable reports, and adversarial mutation suite.
ui.pilot_title: Test one high-risk mutation flow — not your whole company.
ui.pilot_body: Choose one payment, wallet, refund, order, subscription, smart-contract relay, or agent tool mutation where timeout or takeover could create a second effect.
ui.boundary_body: This is a deterministic provider-neutral demonstration. It validates a supplied evidence chain and targeted mutations. It does not prove external exactly-once behavior, provider endorsement, production safety, global completeness, or the absence of every possible duplicate effect. External companies are validation cases — not members or owners of DI, DIF, DRP, or TIP.
ui.footer_role: Independent QA — payment recovery and financial-state verification
ui.unknown_unknown: UNKNOWN means the client still lacks authoritative evidence about the commit outcome. It authorizes recovery or lookup, not a second payment.
ui.unknown_not_committed: NOT_COMMITTED is a positive claim that the effect does not exist. It needs evidence before a retry can be considered safe.

safe.title: DI recovery
safe.decision_note: The committed effect is recovered from authoritative state. A second mutation is blocked.
safe.explanation: Authoritative evidence found the committed effect, so a second mutation is not permitted.

steps.title: Submit one intended payment
steps.detail: The request is bound to one logical operation and one stable effect identity.

steps.title: The financial effect exists
steps.detail: The deterministic sandbox stores exactly one committed effect.

steps.title: The acknowledgement is lost
steps.detail: The client cannot infer commit outcome from a missing transport response.

steps.title: Recover authoritative state
steps.detail: Lookup finds the existing committed effect under the preserved identity.

steps.title: Accept the existing effect
steps.detail: The next action is ACCEPT_EXISTING_EFFECT; duplicate-effect count remains zero.

unsafe.title: Blind retry
unsafe.decision_note: A missing acknowledgement is treated as failure, and recovery mints a fresh mutation identity.
unsafe.explanation: The original commit state was never resolved, so a new mutation can create an additional financial effect.

steps.title: Submit one intended payment
steps.detail: The first request may already have committed at the provider or ledger boundary.

steps.title: The effect may already exist
steps.detail: A server-side commit can happen before the response reaches the client.

steps.title: The acknowledgement is lost
steps.detail: Local transport uncertainty is incorrectly treated as proof of failure.

steps.title: Retry as a fresh mutation
steps.detail: A new request or effect key no longer represents safe recovery of the same operation.

steps.title: A second effect can be created
steps.detail: Without authoritative resolution, duplicate-effect exposure remains open.

search_intents.note: Recover authoritative transaction state before authorizing another financial action.
Keep one logical operation bound to one effect identity across retries.
Block blind retries while the first commit outcome is still unknown.
Require evidence before an autonomous agent can pay again.
